t.6.24.1: Seeing Sītā bewildered, a rākṣasī named Saramā, an affectionate friend, quickly approached her dear Vaidehī.
t.6.24.2: For she, there, had been made a friend by Sītā, who was being kept under guard; protecting her from Rāvaṇa, she was dear to her, compassionate and firm in her vows.
t.6.24.3: Saramā saw her friend Sītā, her senses lost, like a mare that has rolled in the dust and risen again, worn and begrimed.
t.6.24.4: Her friend, faithful to her vows, consoled her with affection: "What you were told by Rāvaṇa, and what you yourself said in reply…"
t.6.24.5: Out of a friend's affection, O timid one, I promised all that, hidden in the deserted thicket and casting aside my fear of Rāvaṇa. It was for your sake, O large-eyed lady, for my own life is not dear to me.
t.6.24.6: The lord of the rākṣasas went out in agitation, and the reason for which he went out, all of that is known to me, O Maithilī, for I went out as well.
t.6.24.8: Nor can the monkeys, who fight with trees, be slain, for they are well protected by Rāma, as the gods are by the foremost of the gods.
t.6.24.7: It is not possible to make a night attack on Rāma, whose nature is well known, and the power of slaying rests with that tiger among men alone.
t.6.24.9: Long and rounded of arm, glorious, broad-chested and majestic, an archer endowed with a well-knit frame, righteous of soul, he is renowned throughout the earth.
t.6.24.10: Valiant, ever the protector of himself and of others, he is well, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, and he is versed in the science of statecraft.
t.6.24.11: O Sītā, the glorious Rāghava, slayer of the hosts of enemy forces, destroyer of foes, whose strength and valor are beyond imagining, has not been slain.
t.6.24.12: This illusion has been worked upon you by that fierce master of illusion, whose mind and deeds are wicked and who is hostile to all beings.
t.6.24.13: All your sorrow is gone; good fortune has come to you. Surely Lakṣmī favors you; hear this pleasing news that will bring you joy.
t.6.24.14: Having crossed the ocean together with the army of monkeys, Rāma reached the southern shore of the sea and encamped there.
t.6.24.15: I have seen Kākutstha together with Lakṣmaṇa, his purpose fulfilled; he stands guarded by the assembled forces stationed at the edge of the ocean.
t.6.24.16: And those swift-paced rākṣasas who were dispatched by him have brought here the news that Rāghava has thus crossed over.
t.6.24.17: O large-eyed one, having heard that news, Rāvaṇa, the lord of the rākṣasas, is here now taking counsel with all his ministers.
t.6.24.18: While the rākṣasī Saramā was speaking thus, she, together with Sītā, heard the terrifying sound of the armies preparing with all their might.
t.6.24.19: Hearing the great sound of the kettledrum resounding under the blows of the drumstick, sweet-spoken Saramā said this to Sītā.
t.6.24.20: O timid one, this dreadful kettledrum indeed calls the warriors to arm themselves; hear the deep sound of the drums, like the rumbling of rain-clouds.
t.6.24.21: Rutting elephants are being equipped, chariot horses are being yoked, and here and there armored foot soldiers are rushing together.
t.6.24.22: The royal highways are being filled with troops of wondrous appearance, swift and roaring, as the ocean is filled with floods of water.
t.6.24.23: Of the gleaming weapons, of shields and of armour, of chariots, horses and elephants, and of the richly adorned rākṣasas.
t.6.24.24: Behold the many-hued radiance rising up from those who send it forth, like the form of fire as it burns down a forest in the hot season.
t.6.24.25: Hear the clanging of the bells, hear the rumbling of the chariots; hear the neighing horses, whose sound is like the blare of trumpets.
t.6.24.26: This tumultuous, hair-raising commotion is that of the Rākṣasas, followers of the lord of the Rākṣasas, with weapons raised in their hands.
t.6.24.27: Śrī, the dispeller of sorrow, is coming to you, O lotus-petal-eyed one; terror has come upon the Rākṣasas from Rāma, as it once came upon the Daityas from Vāsava.
t.6.24.28: Your husband, who has conquered anger and whose valour is beyond imagining, will vanquish Rāvaṇa, slay him in battle, and come to you.
t.6.24.29: Your husband, together with Lakṣmaṇa, will display his valour against the Rākṣasas, just as Vāsava, the slayer of foes, together with Viṣṇu, displays his valour against his enemies.
t.6.24.30: For when the enemy has been struck down, I shall soon see you, your purpose fulfilled, resting in the lap of Rāma who has come.
t.6.24.31: O lovely one, having met him and been embraced upon the chest of that broad-chested one, you will shed tears born of joy.
t.6.24.33: O queen, having seen his face like the full moon risen, you will shed the tears born of grief, as a she-serpent sheds her slough.
t.6.24.32: Before long, O Sītā, O queen, mighty Rāma will loosen this braid of yours, which has hung down to your hips and been worn for many months.
t.6.24.34: O Maithilī, having slain Rāvaṇa in battle before long, he who is worthy of happiness will attain complete happiness together with you, his beloved.
t.6.24.35: United with the great-souled Rāma, you will rejoice, just as the earth rejoices when endowed with good rain and with crops.
t.6.24.36: He who, circling round the best of mountains, swiftly makes his round like a horse, take refuge here in him, O queen, the maker of the day, for he is the source of all creatures.
